turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_data.csv: 300 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, that MAXIMIZES rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) AND stays
robust — its rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) must not collapse under
a ±5% change in any single variable (seek a broad optimum, not a sharp
peak). Design variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
## Analysis of the training data

**Low performers (225–275 MPa):** All have NT=885 with *no* downstream processing (THT=30, CT=30, QmT=30, TT=30 — i.e., essentially as-normalized, no hardening/tempering). Lesson: the full Q&T-style process chain matters enormously.

**Mid performers (325–643 MPa):** NT=825–900 with conventional austenitize–temper cycles (THT≈845–865, THt=30, THQCr=8–24, TT=430–680). Target rises as TT drops (680→580→550→430) and with higher Ni/Cr/Si. Peak here ~900 MPa (C≈0.6, Si≈2.0, TT≈430) — but these sit at extreme corners (max C, max Si, min TT), which is fragile under ±5% perturbation.

**Top performers (838–1190 MPa):** A distinct, internally consistent cluster: NT=930, CT=930 (carburizing-style high-temperature route), Ct=90–540, DT=850–896, Dt=15–70, QmT=60–140, TT=160–200, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, with C≈0.17–0.23, Si≈0.2–0.35, Mn≈0.5–0.85, low P/S, Ni up to ~1.7, Cr≈0.5–1.17, Mo≈0.03–0.24. The single best row (1190) has Ni=1.69, Cr=0.55, Mo=0.18; other >1100 rows have Cr≈1.1–1.17, Ni≈0.5–1.7. So high Ni+Cr+Mo is favorable throughout this cluster.

**Robustness choice:** Within the 930-cluster, the winning variables are *not* at the edge of the feasible ranges (Ct, DT, Dt, QmT all show multiple interior settings with top-10 targets, e.g. Ct=340/470/540, DT=850/896, Dt=15/70, QmT=60/140, TT=160/200 all give ≥1080 MPa). I pick the center of these plateau settings so ±5% moves stay inside the winning regime. I avoid the C=0.6/Si=2.0 spike (sharp corner optimum). Chemistry: keep C low (~0.20, the cluster is uniformly low-C), Si/Mn mid-cluster, Ni and Cr moderately high (multiple top rows share Ni≈1.0–1.7, Cr≈0.9–1.17), Mo≈0.16–0.18, P/S low but not at the absolute floor, RedRatio near 690–860 where many top rows sit, dA/dB/dC low-to-mid.

Final: NT=930, THT=100, THt=10, THQCr=4, CT=930, Ct=450, DT=875, Dt=40, QmT=100, TT=180, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, C=0.20, Si=0.28, Mn=0.70, P=0.012, S=0.014, Ni=1.35, Cr=1.05, Cu=0.10, Mo=0.17, RedRatio=700, dA=0.03, dB=0.01, dC=0.005
